P001.text: Treat a reconstructed applicant scheduling case as the configuration: a fixed application, required orientation and supervised session, applicant availability, instructor and equipment availability, and observed administrative or scheduling conditions that might be changed.

P002.text: These conditions are candidate removable parts; required instruction, safety checks and necessary maintenance remain fixed.

P003.text: First link existing step dates using the minimum identifying information needed, and prospectively record handoffs, contact attempts, prerequisites, offered slots and cancellations.

P004.text: Ask only access-arrangement questions, respect declined contact, and leave unexplained nonresponse unresolved.

P005.text: Before testing, choose a waiting-time threshold and decision horizon.

P006.text: Define failure as permission remaining unavailable beyond that threshold for a fixed applicant; do not improve the result by excluding the applicant or resetting the clock.

P007.text: Whether sufficiently reproducible cases and feasible removable conditions exist is initially unknown.

P008.text: Construct a scheduling replay for selected delayed cases, explicitly documenting assumptions about missing dates, availability and volunteer capacity.

P009.text: Require the unreduced replay to reproduce the documented delay; if it cannot, investigate missing information before reduction.

P010.text: Partition verified, changeable conditions, such as a measured handoff lag or a documented batching rule if one exists.

P011.text: Remove subsets or test their complements by substituting a specified feasible arrangement, while holding the applicant, required steps and other conditions fixed.

P012.text: Retain a reduced configuration only when repeated tests still reproduce the defined failure.

P013.text: Continue partitioning and testing until no single remaining condition can be removed while preserving failure, or until the decision deadline, unresolved outcomes or lack of feasible substitutions stops reduction.

P015.text: A deletion that lacks an operationally feasible counterpart is exploratory only and cannot justify changing arrangements.

P016.text: For each candidate reduction, record failure reproduced, failure absent, or unresolved, alongside predicted permission date, waiting between steps and the remaining blocking conditions.

P017.text: Unknown applicant availability, ambiguous nonresponse or an unsupported scheduling assumption makes the relevant outcome unresolved, not successful or unsuccessful.

P018.text: Repeat tests across plausible uncertain inputs; retain a reduction as robust only if its failure classification remains stable.

P019.text: Where applicants consent and volunteers can support it, test promising arrangements prospectively and compare observed handoff and completion times with replay predictions.

P020.text: No such observations are presumed to have occurred.

P021.text: A retained subset identifies conditions jointly sufficient to reproduce excessive waiting for that applicant under the specified replay and assumptions.

P022.text: If every single deletion has been tested and eliminates failure, it is minimal against those deletions, not necessarily the smallest possible subset.

P023.text: Compare reductions across current and prospective cases to identify recurring delays and how many applicants they affect.

P024.text: Then separately test feasible allocations of the two evening slots to orientation, equipment-specific supervision, or intake coordination where evidence indicates coordination is blocking progress.

P025.text: Test both slots together as well as individually, preserving instructor, equipment and maintenance capacity.

P026.text: Use predicted reductions in excessive waits, confirmed where possible by prospective results, to choose next month's allocation.

P027.text: A retained condition alone does not establish that adding a session will help.

P028.text: If evidence remains weak, make any allocation a limited monitored trial with a specified review date.

P029.text: Replaying the same assumptions repeatedly establishes computational repeatability, not real-world reproducibility.

P030.text: Historical reconstruction alone cannot establish the effects of changed arrangements.

P031.text: Interactions, cancellations, changing demand, applicant availability, missing records and the order of reductions can produce different retained subsets.

P032.text: Separate spreadsheets and monthly totals may support only partial reconstruction; do not force a minimal result from unresolved tests.

P033.text: Reductions from selected cases do not establish the largest source of delay across the queue, a unique cause, or guaranteed benefits from extra sessions.

P034.text: If prospective outcomes contradict predictions, revise the reconstruction and retest.

P035.text: Stop any trial that would compromise required instruction, safety checks or necessary maintenance; stop contacting an applicant who declines, and retain their unexplained delay as unknown rather than treating it as resolved.
